skill.name: crud-with-spec-kit
skill.description: Guides AI-assisted CRUD implementation from Spec-Kit feature specifications, including backend routes, frontend clients, tests, and validation checks.
skill.summary: Plan and validate CRUD features from Spec-Kit specifications.
skill.author: Claude

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns in the single prompt-only skill file. Manual semantic review found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable behavior; no remediation is required.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time translating specifications into consistent CRUD implementations. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through spec analysis, scaffolding, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Interprets Spec-Kit feature files for entities, attributes, relationships, operations, constraints, and success criteria.
Maps CRUD requirements to backend routes, request models, response formats, and error handling.
Guides frontend client and UI component scaffolding for CRUD workflows.
Promotes validation checks that compare generated behavior against the specification.
Outlines testing, documentation, and quality review steps for generated CRUD features.
limitations: It is conceptual guidance, not a packaged generator or executable tool.
It depends on clear Spec-Kit files and project-specific implementation choices.
It does not cover complex domain logic beyond basic CRUD patterns.
Generated code still needs human review, security checks, and framework-specific tests.

use_cases.title: Create REST endpoints from specs
use_cases.description: Convert entity definitions and success criteria into consistent create, read, update, and delete route plans.

use_cases.title: Build CRUD clients and screens
use_cases.description: Use backend entity contracts to plan typed clients, forms, lists, and state patterns.

use_cases.title: Audit implementation coverage
use_cases.description: Compare completed CRUD work against Spec-Kit requirements and identify missing validation or tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a CRUD feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the crud-with-spec-kit skill to read my Spec-Kit feature file and summarize entities, operations, constraints, and missing details.

prompt_templates.title: Generate backend scaffolding
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design backend CRUD routes from the specification. Include validation, error handling, response expectations, and testing notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create frontend integration plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to map the backend CRUD contract into frontend clients, forms, list views, state handling, and user feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Validate spec compliance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare the implementation against the Spec-Kit success criteria. Report gaps, risks, and recommended follow-up tests.

output_examples.input: Spec file for a task management feature with task entities and CRUD requirements.
output: Backend route plan with validation notes

output_examples.input: Existing CRUD implementation that must be checked against Spec-Kit success criteria.
output: Missing validation and error handling items
Suggested tests for create, read, update, and delete flows

best_practices: Provide complete Spec-Kit files before asking for scaffolding.
Review generated code for authorization, validation, and data integrity before release.
Keep success criteria linked to tests and implementation tasks.
anti_patterns: Using the skill when entity relationships or constraints are still undefined.
Accepting generated CRUD code without framework-specific tests.
Forcing complex workflows into basic CRUD patterns without domain review.

faq.question: Does this skill generate executable code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It gives structured guidance for AI-assisted implementation in the user's project.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: A clear Spec-Kit feature file with entities, constraints, operations, and success criteria works best.

faq.question: Can it support frontend and backend work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers backend routes, frontend clients, UI patterns, tests, and validation review.

faq.question: Is it limited to REST APIs?
faq.answer: The skill focuses on REST-style CRUD patterns, but users can adapt the guidance to similar API designs.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. Generated CRUD code still needs authorization, input validation, and project-specific security checks.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers and technical leads who turn stable product specifications into CRUD features should use it.
